event_date_basis: The announcement page itself (sources[0], read directly today with HTTP 200, not via any archive) carries its own byline 'March 31, 2026' immediately under the OpenAI byline, filed under the category 'Company', and opens 'Today, we closed our latest funding round...'. The close and the announcement therefore share the same date, 2026-03-31. This is distinct from the money-in dates: SoftBank's own releases show its first USD 10.0bn tranche executed 2026-04-01 (referenced by title in the 2026-07-01 release used as sources[2]), the second executed 2026-07-01, and a third planned for 2026-10-01; Amazon's own release (sources[3], dated 2026-02-27) splits its $50bn into an initial $15bn and a later $35bn. news_date and the slug date are 2026-03-31, the announcement/close date, not any of these background or payment dates.

sourcing_notes: 2026-09-18, all four sources[] URLs fetched directly with curl -sL -A "Mokaair-editorial" (no email or personal data in any request) and read to the article body, not just a 200 status. openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/ -> HTTP 200, 375,656 bytes; this is a change from the 403 Cloudflare block this project's prior research recorded on 2026-09-16, so the block that made must_fix 5's Wayback question live appears to have been lifted since then -- confirmed genuine by matching <title> ('OpenAI raises $122 billion to accelerate the next phase of AI | OpenAI') and og:description against OpenAI's own RSS description fetched the same session. No web.archive.org URL was used anywhere in this pass. group.softbank/en/news/press/20260227 -> HTTP 200, 206,950 bytes, full press-release body including the tranche table. group.softbank/en/news/press/20260701 -> HTTP 200, 193,924 bytes, confirms the second tranche executed and references the April 1 first-tranche release by title. press.aboutamazon.com/2026/2/openai-and-amazon-announce-strategic-partnership -> HTTP 200, 155,750 bytes, full release with both executive quotes. Two further URLs were read directly (HTTP 200) purely as corroboration, not as sources[] entries because no article sentence is pinned to them: openai.com/news/rss.xml (confirms the canonical link/guid and the pubDate Tue, 31 Mar 2026 13:00:00 GMT for this item, and separately carries OpenAI's own confidential-S-1 item dated Mon, 08 Jun 2026 14:00:00 GMT, consistent with the second article's slug date) and openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ (confirms the canonical <loc> and a zh-Hant hreflang alternate for this same URL, itself returning 403 and therefore not read). nvidianews.nvidia.com/releases.xml was re-fetched (HTTP 200) and still does not reach back to March 2026, independently re-confirming that no NVIDIA amount can be sourced. No claim in the article or in verified_facts rests on a media outlet, aggregator, or archived page; sources[] entries 2-4 replace the prior research's reliance on the 2026-04-01 SoftBank release with the 2026-02-27 release (which already carries the full three-tranche schedule and the pre-money valuation) plus the 2026-07-01 release (added, to show two of the three tranches as actually executed rather than only planned).

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI's announcement page carries its own byline 'March 31, 2026' directly under the OpenAI name, filed under the category 'Company'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote:
OpenAI
March 31, 2026
Company

verified_facts.fact: The page's headline is 'OpenAI raises $122 billion to accelerate the next phase of AI'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI raises $122 billion to accelerate the next phase of AI

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it closed the round that day with $122 billion in committed capital at a post-money valuation of $852 billion; the post's own wording is 'committed capital', not cash received.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today, we closed our latest funding round with $122 billion in committed capital at a post money valuation of $852 billion.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says the round was anchored by strategic partners Amazon, NVIDIA and SoftBank, with continued participation from long-term partner Microsoft; SoftBank co-led alongside a16z, D. E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG, and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. No dollar amount is given for any of these investors anywhere in the post.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The round was anchored by our strategic partners Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank, with continued participation from our long-term partner, Microsoft. SoftBank co-led the round alongside a16z, D. E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG, and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says there was 'significant participation from a diverse set of global institutions including' a named list (Altimeter, Appaloosa LP, ARK Invest, funds affiliated with BlackRock, Blackstone, Coatue and others). 'Including' marks this as a non-exhaustive list, not the full roster of participants.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: There was also significant participation from a diverse set of global institutions including Altimeter, Appaloosa LP, ARK Invest, affiliated funds of BlackRock, Blackstone, Coatue

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says that for the first time it extended participation to investors through bank channels, raising over $3 billion from individual investors. No bank or channel is named, and no country list is given.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: For the first time, we extended participation to investors through bank channels, raising over $3 billion from individual investors.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is also announcing that OpenAI will be included in several exchange-traded funds managed by ARK Invest. No fund name, ticker or inclusion date is given.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today, we’re also announcing that OpenAI will be included in several exchange-traded funds managed by ARK Invest

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says ChatGPT is 'the overwhelming leader in consumer AI' with more than 900 million weekly active users and over 50 million subscribers. No definition of 'weekly active user' or 'subscriber' is given.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: ChatGPT is the overwhelming leader in consumer AI with more than 900 million weekly active users, and over 50 million subscribers.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it was the fastest technology platform to reach 10 million users and 100 million users, and will soon be the fastest to reach 1 billion weekly active users. No date is given for the 1-billion milestone.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI was the fastest technology platform to reach 10 million users, the fastest to 100 million users, and soon the fastest to 1 billion weekly active users.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it reached $1B in revenue within a year of launching ChatGPT, was generating $1B per quarter by the end of 2024, and is now generating $2B in revenue per month.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Within a year of launching ChatGPT, we reached $1B in revenue. By the end of 2024 we were generating $1B per quarter. We are now generating $2B in revenue per month.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says that at this stage it is growing revenue four times faster than 'the companies who defined the Internet and mobile eras, including Alphabet and Meta'. Alphabet and Meta are given as examples inside a larger, unnamed comparison set (via 'including'), not as a one-to-one benchmark; the article does not narrow this into 'four times faster than Alphabet and Meta'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: At this stage, we are growing revenue four times faster than the companies who defined the Internet and mobile eras, including Alphabet and Meta.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says ChatGPT has 6x the monthly web visits and mobile sessions of the next-largest AI app, that total AI time spent is 4x the next-largest AI app and 4x all other apps combined, that search usage has 'nearly tripled in a year', and that its ads pilot reached more than $100 million in ARR in under six weeks. No measurement source is named for any of these comparisons.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: ChatGPT has 6x the monthly web visits and mobile sessions than the next largest AI app, while total AI time spent is 4x the next largest AI app and 4x all others combined. Search usage has nearly tripled in a year, and our ads pilot reached more than $100 million in ARR in under six weeks.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says enterprise now makes up more than 40% of its revenue and is on track to reach parity with consumer revenue by the end of 2026.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Momentum is just as strong on the enterprise side, which now makes up more than 40% of our revenue, and is on track to reach parity with consumer by the end of 2026.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says its APIs now process more than 15 billion tokens per minute, and that Codex serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in the past three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our APIs now process more than 15 billion tokens per minute. Codex now serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in the past three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI describes its infrastructure portfolio as spanning cloud through Microsoft, Oracle, AWS, CoreWeave and Google Cloud; silicon through NVIDIA, AMD, AWS Trainium, Cerebras and its own chip built in partnership with Broadcom; and data centers through partnerships with Oracle, SBE and SoftBank.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: This strategy now spans: cloud through Microsoft, Oracle, AWS, CoreWeave, and Google Cloud; silicon through NVIDIA, AMD, AWS Trainium, Cerebras, and our own chip in partnership with Broadcom; and data centers through partnerships with Oracle, SBE, and SoftBank.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says Nvidia 'remains the foundation of our infrastructure', that its training fleet and the majority of its inference stack continue to run on Nvidia GPUs, and that this funding round deepens that partnership.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Nvidia remains the foundation of our infrastructure. Our training fleet and the majority of our inference stack continue to run on Nvidia GPUs, and with this round we are deepening that partnership as we scale.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI's own explanation for why compute spending matters: new generations of infrastructure train more capable models, while algorithmic and hardware improvements reduce the cost to serve each token. The post attaches no figure, date or product promise to this argument, and makes no promise about ChatGPT's speed, price or usage limits anywhere in the text.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With each new generation of infrastructure, we train more capable models, making each token more intelligent than before. At the same time, algorithmic and hardware improvements reduce the cost to serve each token, lowering the cost per unit of intelligence.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI's post mentions in passing that it 'recently launched GPT‑5.4' and expanded Codex into a coding agent, and separately expanded into health, scientific discovery and commerce; the source page prints the model name with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011), not an ASCII hyphen.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: We recently launched GPT‑5.4, our most capable model yet, with meaningful gains in intelligence and workflow performance. We expanded Codex into a flagship coding agent.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is building a unified AI 'superapp' that will bring together ChatGPT, Codex, browsing and its broader agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience. No launch date, product name, price, plan tier or region is given anywhere in the post, and it does not say whether the existing separate apps will be merged or retired.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our superapp will bring together ChatGPT, Codex, browsing, and our broader agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI frames the superapp as a response to usability, not capability: as models get more capable, it says, the limiting factor shifts from intelligence to usability.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: As models become more capable, the limiting factor shifts from intelligence to usability.

editorial_brief: Written for a Taiwanese reader who already uses ChatGPT and keeps seeing large AI funding numbers without knowing whether any of it changes the product on their phone. The angle is deliberately not investment: what does the announcement promise a user, and what does it pointedly not promise. Four threads: (1) the headline numbers, attributed as OpenAI's own claims -- $122bn committed capital, $852bn post-money, 900M+ weekly users, 50M+ subscribers, revenue figures, all framed as OpenAI 表示; (2) the gap between 'committed capital' and cash in hand, shown with two independent first-party examples -- SoftBank's $30bn arriving as three $10bn tranches (two confirmed executed by the check date, the third not yet due) and Amazon's $50bn split into $15bn now plus $35bn later under undisclosed conditions; (3) what the money funds (compute/infrastructure) and what it explicitly does not buy the reader -- no promised change to ChatGPT's speed, price or limits, illustrated with a labelled editorial example; (4) the 'superapp' plan and the open questions, including a brief, non-speculative note on the IPO-linked mechanics in SoftBank's own preferred-share terms, pointing to the separate S-1 article rather than re-covering it. Deliberately out of scope: valuation analysis, whether or how to invest, IPO prediction, market/share-price commentary, and re-explaining GPT-5.4, GPT-6 Astra or the Agents API (link out instead).
must_not_write: Do not write that ChatGPT will become faster, cheaper, have higher limits, or gain any specific new feature because of this funding; the announcement promises none of it.
Do not give the superapp a launch date, name, price, plan tier or region, and do not say existing apps will be retired or merged on any timetable.
Do not attribute a dollar amount to NVIDIA or Microsoft; no first-party source reached gives one.
Do not state what Amazon's 'certain conditions' for the second $35 billion are, and in particular do not write 'IPO or AGI'.
Do not call it the largest funding round in history, a record, or any similar superlative.
Do not present $122 billion as money OpenAI received on 2026-03-31; it is committed capital, and SoftBank's and Amazon's own releases show it arriving over time.
Do not suggest, imply or explain how a reader could invest in OpenAI; do not say Taiwanese readers can participate through banks or ETFs; name no ARK ticker.
Do not predict an IPO, a listing date or a venue; the only first-party material is deal mechanics (conversion and acceleration clauses) that exist regardless of whether or when a listing happens.
Do not write OpenAI's self-reported metrics as independently established fact; every one of them is OpenAI 表示 / OpenAI 說.
Do not write that this site tested or independently verified any of these numbers.
Do not re-explain GPT-5.4, GPT-6 Astra or the Agents API; the site already has articles on each, and this post mentions GPT-5.4 only in passing.
Do not claim any Chinese wording is OpenAI's official translation; the zh-Hant page was not read in this check.
Do not put a number in the diagram, hero label or summary that does not also appear in the body paragraphs.
Do not use the 2026-02-27 SoftBank or Amazon dates as the event date; the event date is 2026-03-31, and the February dates are clearly marked as earlier background in the article.
Do not add the SoftBank and Amazon dollar figures together or otherwise imply they account for the full $122 billion; about $42 billion of the total has no first-party breakdown.
